image.prompt:
Straight-on ELEVATION photograph of one whole high-rise building, taken from very far away with a long telephoto lens: the camera is level with the building's mid-height, so every vertical edge is perfectly vertical and parallel with no keystone convergence, and the main facade is seen frontally with only a thin sliver of one side. Not a three-quarter view, not an aerial view, not looking up from the street.

The building: Two identical fifty-storey office towers side by side on a shared four-storey retail podium, green-tinted curtain wall with white horizontal spandrel bands on every floor, a glazed sky bridge linking the towers near the top, flat roofs with white helipads and rooftop plant screens Materials: green-tinted reflective curtain wall, white aluminium spandrel bands, grey concrete podium with a tiled facade, white helipad markings on grey roofs.

Whole building: the complete tower from its ground-floor base to the very top of its crown, roof plant, spire or antenna, with nothing cropped. The base sits at the bottom of the silhouette with nothing in front of it: no trees, no street, no cars, no people, no neighbouring buildings, no scaffolding. The only text is lettering explicitly described above; otherwise no signs, no logos, no watermarks, no annotations.

Framing: the building is centred and fills about 85% of the frame along its longer axis, with a clear empty margin on every side.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080) fills every part of the frame that is not the building, including where the sky would be and where the ground would be. The building is a cut-out floating against an infinite flat backdrop. No sky, no clouds, no horizon, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient, no haze, no atmospheric fade.

Lighting: bright overcast daylight, flat and even, soft and shadowless, so the facade reads as true albedo with its glass tint, concrete and paint colours exactly as described. No sun glare, no specular blowout, no lens flare, no dramatic sky colour reflected in the glass.

One building only. Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, every floor, window, mullion and balcony resolved, realistic weathering and grime. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render, not a wireframe, not low-poly.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Twin Office Towers with Sky Bridge
nameTh: ตึกแฝดสะพานลอยฟ้า
notes: One imposter, two towers: they share one quad on purpose because the sky bridge joins them, and splitting them would need two billboards that yaw apart. Declared width is the pair with the podium. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 2:3, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand.
